papers.title_in_file: Experimental signature of programmable quantum annealing
papers.version_note: The file is the arXiv:1212.1739v1 preprint dated 7 December 2012 (12 pages), not the later journal version the record id year (2013) suggests.
sections_read: Main text (unnumbered introduction, classical thermalization prediction, quantum annealing prediction, experiment, robustness checks, annealing-time test, conclusion, Acknowledgements)
Appendix A: First-principles derivation of the master equation
Appendix B: Correlation functions and the KMS condition
Appendix C: Spectrum and ground states of the Ising Hamiltonian
Appendix D: Simulated annealing and classical thermalization
Appendix E: Classical master equation explanation for the enhancement of the isolated state
Appendix F: Degenerate perturbation theory explanation for quantum suppression of the isolated state
Appendix G: The quantum Singular Coupling Limit does not agree with the experimental results

papers.what_it_is: A 2012 arXiv preprint reporting D-Wave One experiments on an 8-qubit Ising problem with a 17-fold degenerate ground state, in which the isolated ground state is suppressed as open-system quantum annealing predicts and classical thermalization does not.

assertions.value: The authors state that, using superconducting flux qubits with programmable spin-spin couplings, they establish an experimental signature consistent with quantum annealing and inconsistent with classical thermalization, in spite of a decoherence timescale orders of magnitude shorter than the adiabatic evolution time.
quotes: using superconducting ﬂux qubits with programmable spin-spin couplings

an experimental signature which is consistent with quantum annealing, and at the same time inconsistent with classical thermalization, in spite of a decoherence timescale which is orders of magnitude shorter than the adiabatic evolution time.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one device and one Hamiltonian.

assertions.value: The authors define the quantum annealing Hamiltonian as H(t) = A(t)Htrans + B(t)HIsing, t ∈ [0, T ], where the annealing schedule satisfies A(0), B(T ) > 0 and A(T ) = B(0) = 0.
quotes: H(t) = A(t)Htrans + B(t)HIsing, t ∈ [0, T ],
satisﬁes A(0), B(T ) > 0 and A(T ) = B(0) = 0.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own definition of the annealing Hamiltonian and schedule conditions.

assertions.value: The authors state that, if the change is sufficiently slow, the adiabatic theorem of quantum mechanics predicts that the system will remain in its ground state and an optimal solution is obtained.
quotes: If the change is suﬃciently slow, the adiabatic theorem of quantum mechanics predicts that the system will remain in its ground state, and an optimal solution is obtained
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper attributes it to cited work.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper cites two references for this statement.

assertions.value: The authors state that similar transformations with more general Hamiltonians are equivalent in computational power, up to polynomial overhead, to the standard circuit model of quantum computation.
quotes: Similar transformations with more general Hamiltonians are equivalent in computational power (up to polynomial overhead) to the standard circuit model of quantum computation
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that such transformations offer at least a quadratic speed-up over any classical SA algorithm.
quotes: and oﬀer at least a quadratic speed-up over any classical SA algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.
assertions.reader_inference: The sentence concerns the more general Hamiltonians named just before it, not the specific device used in the experiments.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in the circuit model of quantum computation, a relatively short decoherence time would imply without quantum error correction that the system dynamics can be described by classical laws.
quotes: this relatively short decoherence time would imply, without quantum error correction
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement the paper supports with citations.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper states the full claim as: that the system dynamics can be described by classical laws, after the quoted fragment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the decoherence time in this superconducting flux-qubit architecture can be three orders of magnitude faster than the computational timescale, due in part to the constraints imposed by the scalable design.
quotes: the decoherence time in this architecture can be three orders of magnitude faster than the computational timescale, due in part to the constraints imposed by the scalable design.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement without a measurement in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that many optimization problems can be naturally expressed as the NP-hard problem of finding the ground state, or minimum energy configuration, of an Ising spin glass model.
quotes: Many optimization problems can be naturally expressed as the NP-hard problem of ﬁnding the ground state, or minimum energy conﬁguration, of an Ising spin glass model
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement the paper supports with citations.

assertions.value: The authors state that their eight-qubit Ising Hamiltonian, depicted in Fig. 1, has a 17-fold degenerate ground state.
quotes: We answer this by studying an eight-qubit Hamiltonian representing a simple optimization problem
Our Ising Hamiltonian, depicted in Fig. 1, has a 17-fold degenerate ground state
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup; Appendix C derives the degeneracy.

assertions.value: The authors state that sixteen of the ground states form a cluster connected by single spin-flips of the ancillae spins, while the seventeenth ground state is isolated and can be reached only after at least four spin-flips of the core spins.
quotes: Sixteen of these states form a cluster of solutions connected by single spin-ﬂips of the ancillae spins [Eq. (4a)]
the seventeenth ground state is isolated from this cluster in the sense that it can be reached only after at least four spin-ﬂips of the core spins [Eq. (4b)]
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the structure of its own test Hamiltonian; Appendix C derives it.

assertions.value: The authors define pi as the probability of state i in the cluster and ps as the probability of the isolated state, and consider the average cluster probability pC.
quotes: Let pi denote the probability of state i in the cluster (4a), and ps the probability of the isolated state (4b).
so we consider the average cluster probability
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own definitions.

assertions.value: The authors state that classical thermalization predicts that the isolated solution will be found with higher probability than any of the cluster solutions, that is, it is enhanced.
quotes: classical thermalization predicts that the isolated solution will be found with higher probability than any of the cluster solutions, i.e., it is enhanced.
assertions.certainty_reason: A prediction supported by an approximate rate-equation argument and simulations under stated assumptions.

assertions.value: The authors state that open system QA makes the opposite prediction: after an initial transient the isolated solution is suppressed relative to the cluster, and faster quantum dynamics yields higher suppression.
quotes: Open system QA makes the exact opposite prediction: after an initial transient, the isolated solution is suppressed relative to the cluster, and faster quantum dynamics yields higher suppression (lower probability).
assertions.certainty_reason: A prediction supported by perturbation arguments and simulations; the text calls it confirmed by simulations, not proved.

assertions.value: The authors state that the isolated state is connected via single spin-flips to 8 excited states with energy −4, while all states in the cluster are connected via single spin-flips to at most 4 singly-excited states.
quotes: to 8 excited states with energy −4
all states in the cluster are connected via single spin-ﬂips to at most
4 singly-excited states

assertions.value: The authors state that they derive from first principles, within the open quantum systems formalism, the master equation used by SA, and obtain the detailed balance condition for thermalization dynamics.
assertions.anchor: Appendix A, p.4; Appendix A, p.6
quotes: Here we derive the master equation used by SA from ﬁrst principles within the open quantum systems formalism.
gives the detailed balance condition for thermalization dynamics
assertions.certainty_reason: The derivation is given in Appendix A under the assumptions quoted in the separate assumption assertions (rotating wave approximation, a specific system-bath coupling form, a thermal bath).

assertions.value: The paper proves that, for a bath whose correlation function satisfies the KMS condition, is analytic in the strip between τ = −iβ and τ = 0, and vanishes at infinite time, the Fourier transform of the bath correlation function satisfies the detailed balance condition Eq. (A4).
quotes: The correlation function of a thermal bath is assumed to satisfy the KMS (Kubo-Martin-Schwinger) condition

If in addition the correlation function is analytic in the strip between τ = −iβ and τ = 0, then it follows that the Fourier transform of the bath correlation function satisﬁes the detailed balance condition Eq. (A4) as we show next.

assertions.value: The authors state that they are interested in sufficiently slow thermalization processes, relative to spin flip rates, so that states connected by single spin-flips have similar populations, and that the cluster of 16 degenerate ground states and the isolated ground state are connected via a plateau of excited states with energy −4.
quotes: We are interested in suﬃciently slow thermalization processes (relative to spin ﬂip rates), so that states connected by single spin-ﬂips have similar populations.
The cluster of 16 degenerate ground states and the isolated ground state are connected via a plateau of excited states with energy −4.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the regime and structure its derivation covers.

assertions.value: The authors derive for the isolated state the rate equation p˙s = 8f (−4)pe − 8f (4)ps, where pe is the population of the excited states with energy −4, assuming the spin flip rate is the same for all sites.
quotes: p˙s = 8f (−4)pe − 8f (4)ps
where pe is the population of the excited states with energy −4.
Here we are assuming that the spin ﬂip
rate is the same for all sites
assertions.certainty_reason: Appendix E derives it by counting the eight single-spin-flip transitions, with the equal-rate assumption quoted.

assertions.value: The authors state that a cluster state with l ancillae with spin ↓ and 4 − l ancillae with spin ↑ connects via single spin-flips to l excited states with energy −4 and 4−l excited states with energy 0.
quotes: Thus, a state with l ancillae with spin ↓ and 4 − l ancillae with spin ↑ connects (via single spin-ﬂips) to l excited states with energy −4 and 4−l excited states with energy 0.
assertions.certainty_reason: Appendix E derives it from the core-ancilla pair energies of Appendix C.

assertions.value: The authors state that, to write a rate equation for pC, they assume that all excited states with energy 0 (−4) have probability p(0) (pe) and that all states in the ground state cluster have equal probability pC.
quotes: we shall assume that all excited states with energy 0 (−4) have probability p(0) (pe), and all states in the ground state cluster have equal probability pC
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states an assumption of its own derivation.

assertions.value: The authors state that for most temperatures of interest the dominant transitions are those between the cluster and states with energy -4, giving the approximation p˙C ≈ 2f (−4) pe − 2f (4) pC.
quotes: the dominant transitions are those between the cluster and states with energy -4.
p˙C ≈ 2f (−4) pe − 2f (4) pC
assertions.certainty_reason: An approximation whose neglected terms are argued small, not bounded.

assertions.value: The authors derive, starting from ps ≥ pC holding initially and from the assumption that the excited to ground probability ratio is not lower than its thermal equilibrium value, that p˙s − p˙C ≥ 0 when ps and pC become equal, implying that at all times ps ≥ pC.
quotes: To show that ps ≥ pC , assume that this is indeed the case initially.
p˙s − p˙C ≥ 0 ,
implying that at all times ps ≥ pC .
assertions.certainty_reason: The argument rests on the approximate cluster rate equation and a non-equilibrium ratio assumption.
assertions.reader_inference: Appendix E's first sentence says the isolated-state probability never exceeds the cluster average, but the inequality it states and proves is ps ≥ pC, which is the opposite direction; the intended meaning is that ps never falls below the average.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because the SA process proceeds via cooling, the ratio between the non-equilibrium excited state and the ground state probabilities will not be lower than the corresponding thermal equilibrium transition ratio.
quotes: the ratio between the non-equilibrium excited state and the ground state probabilities will not be lower than the corresponding thermal equilibrium
assertions.certainty_reason: A physical assumption stated without proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that the isolated state is unconnected via single spin flips to any other state in the ground subspace, and that the transverse field splits the ground space of HIsing, with none of the lowered states overlapping the isolated ground state.
quotes: The isolated state is unconnected via single spin ﬂips to any other state in the ground subspace
None of these states overlaps with the isolated ground state, which is therefore not a ground state of the perturbed Hamiltonian.
assertions.certainty_reason: Appendix F derives it by degenerate perturbation theory with the transverse field as a perturbation, a condition the paper states.

assertions.value: The authors state that after the perturbation only the sixth excited state overlaps with the isolated state, and that the isolated state becomes a ground state only at the very end of the evolution, when the perturbation has vanished.
quotes: after the perturbation, only the sixth excited state overlaps with the isolated state.
The isolated state becomes a ground state only at the very end of the evolution (with time going forward), when the perturbation has vanished.
assertions.certainty_reason: Appendix F derives it by degenerate perturbation theory, stating the perturbative setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that an open system QA master equation in the singular coupling limit yields results in qualitative agreement with classical thermalization, and opposite to their weak coupling limit master equation.
quotes: Interestingly, an open system QA master equation in the singular coupling limit (SCL) yields results in qualitative agreement with classical thermalization, and opposite to our weak coupling limit (WCL) master equation (A1).
assertions.certainty_reason: A simulation and derivation result under limit assumptions the paper later argues do not match the experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SCL master equation predicts that the isolated state is enhanced relative to the cluster of states, in contradiction to their experimental findings.
quotes: Namely, the SCL master equation predicts that the isolated state is enhanced relative to the cluster of states.
in contradiction to our experimental ﬁndings.
assertions.certainty_reason: A theoretical prediction compared with one device's data.

assertions.value: The authors state that, since the bath and system-bath coupling dominate the system Hamiltonian in the SCL, it predicts that decoherence takes place not in the instantaneous energy eigenbasis of the system but in the computational basis.
quotes: Since the bath and system-bath coupling dominate the system Hamiltonian in the SCL, it predicts that decoherence takes place not in the instantaneous energy eigenbasis of the system but in the computational basis.
assertions.certainty_reason: A theoretical consequence of the SCL, stated without a separate proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that the agreement between their experimental results and the WCL master equation supports the idea that decoherence takes place in the instantaneous energy eigenbasis of the system and/or that the Lamb shift does not dominate the system Hamiltonian.
quotes: The agreement we ﬁnd between our experimental results and the WCL master equation instead supports the idea that decoherence takes place in the instantaneous energy eigenbasis of the system and/or that the Lamb shift does not dominate the system Hamiltonian.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author interpretation of the data.

assertions.value: The authors report that the concurrence of the states obtained from their master equation during the QA evolution is finite, and state that this suggests entanglement is being generated in their experiments.
quotes: we ﬁnd it to be ﬁnite, as seen in Fig. 11.
This suggests that entanglement is being generated in our experiments.
assertions.certainty_reason: A simulation result with an author inference about the experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that answering the entanglement question experimentally requires measurements during the annealing, a capability that is absent from the device used in their experiments.
quotes: Answering this question experimentally requires measurements to be performed during the annealing, a capability that is absent from the device used in our experiments.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state a limit of their own device.
